newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg/mark to use 2.8650 as base for gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg/mark to use 2.8650 as base for gains.

text.p: Sterling will use 2.8650 marks as a base from which to push up to new 59-month highs in the coming days, analysts said on Tuesday.
Cable will struggle to keep up with gains the pound makes against the mark, but needs to hold above $1.6650/60 if traders are to remain optimistic about its prospects, they said.

"In the short term, there is still some upward momentum and scope for a move back up towards 2.8750 marks," said Robin Poynder, chief foreign exchange trader at Charterhouse. "2.8650 will act as the short-term support, and as long as 2.8550 holds further out, the uptrend will remain intact."

Sterling rose to a new 59-month high of 2.9740 marks early in Europe, its best showing since July 1992. It was quoted at 2.8735/45 marks at 0750 GMT, compared with 2.8725/35 late Monday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6668/78 from $1.6682/92 late yesterday.

Howard Wright, chief analyst at Prisma Market Analysts, said he expects sterling/mark to find 2.8750 a major hurdle and said the pound could pull back to 2.8485 marks if it proves unable to break above this level.
A move above 2.8650 marks would, however, pave the way for sterling gains to above 2.89 marks, analysts said.
Cable will struggle to perform as well as sterling/mark, but could make a renewed bid to break above $1.6730 as long as $1.6650/60 remains intact, analysts said.
Sterling rose on Monday as high as $1.6725, the strongest it has been since January 17.
"The $1.6650 level, which was the old resistance, is now acting as support," said Poynder at Charterhouse.
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 66 pct, Stg/dollar: 68 pct
